title: Why Value Investors Are Watching Infosys Ahead of Q1 Results
excerpt: With the stock trading near 52-week lows and a Zacks 'Buy' rating, Infosys presents a compelling valuation case — but headwinds from tariff uncertainty and deal ramp-downs complicate the picture.
body:
• Infosys (INFY) trades near its 52-week low with a trailing P/E of 14.4x and a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with Value Grade 'A,' suggesting the stock may be undervalued relative to industry peers.
  • The company reports Q1 FY27 results on July 23, with brokerages projecting revenue of ₹48,086–48,659 crore and constant-currency growth of 2–2.2% sequentially.
  • Analysts remain divided on FY27 guidance, with expectations ranging from a trimmed 1.5–3% to an upgraded 2–4%, depending on organic growth momentum and acquisition contributions.

A Value Stock in Plain Sight?

Infosys, India's second-largest IT services company, is drawing renewed attention from value investors as its American depositary receipts languish near 52-week lows. The stock closed at $11.52 on the NYSE on July 17, well below its 52-week high of $30.00 — a decline of more than 60% from its peak.

With the company set to report June-quarter earnings on July 23, the valuation debate has intensified. Zacks Investment Research flagged Infosys as potentially undervalued in a late-June analysis, awarding it a Rank #2 (Buy) alongside a top-tier Value Style Score of 'A.'

The numbers back the thesis. Infosys trades at a price-to-book ratio of 6.33, a steep discount to its IT services industry average of 17.57. Its trailing P/E of 14.39 and forward P/E of 14.04 sit below historical medians, while the company carries zero long-term debt and generates a return on equity of 32.64%.

Q1 Preview: Steady but Not Spectacular

Brokerage estimates for Q1 FY27 point to a quarter of incremental progress rather than a breakout. Revenue is expected in the range of ₹48,086 crore to ₹48,659 crore, translating to sequential constant-currency growth of approximately 2–2.2%. On a year-on-year basis, reported revenue is projected to climb 13.7–14.9%, boosted by recent acquisitions.

Infosys completed its acquisition of Stratus in the March quarter and is expected to close the Optimum Healthcare IT deal, which together should contribute roughly 120 basis points to inorganic revenue growth. Motilal Oswal Financial Services noted that the IT major may lead large-cap growth this quarter, supported by these deals and ongoing cost efficiencies under Project Maximus.

Operating margins are forecast to improve 20–40 basis points sequentially to approximately 21.2–21.4%, aided by the absence of wage hikes and reversal of visa costs from the prior quarter.

"The 1.5–3.5% FY27 guidance sits below the 3.1% Infosys just delivered and is an unusual stance given the deal book strength, and a tacit acknowledgement that EUR programme ramp-down, tariff uncertainty in manufacturing, and the West Asia exposure are real near-term drags."

— Sidhant Rastogi, President, Zinnov

The Guidance Question

The key earnings-day catalyst will be whether management revises its FY27 revenue growth guidance of 1.5–3.5% in constant-currency terms. Brokerages are split: Motilal Oswal expects a 50-basis-point trim at the upper end, bringing the range to 1.5–3%. BNP Paribas, by contrast, anticipates an upgrade to 2–4% to reflect the Optimum acquisition's contribution.

Elara Securities warned that a weaker-than-usual Q1 — historically, Infosys posts average sequential CC growth above 3% in the June quarter — would create "risk on the upper end of the FY27 revenue growth target."

For the full year ended March 2026, Infosys posted revenue of ₹1,78,650 crore (up 9.6% YoY) and net profit of ₹29,440 crore (up 10.2%). Large deal total contract value stood at $14.9 billion, with 55% classified as net new business.

What Diaspora Investors Should Watch

For NRI and diaspora investors who hold Infosys through its NYSE ADR — one of the most liquid Indian equity instruments available globally — the July 23 earnings call carries outsized importance. The Wall Street consensus stands at 7 hold ratings against 1 buy and 1 sell, with an average price target of $12.50, implying roughly 8.6% upside from current levels.

Beyond the headline numbers, three factors will shape the stock's trajectory: the pace at which Infosys's $14.9 billion deal pipeline converts to revenue, the extent to which AI-related engagements appear in formal bookings disclosures, and whether the Daimler contract ramp-down and telecom sector weakness persist through the quarter.

At a trailing P/E below 15x and free cash flow conversion above 112% of net profit, Infosys offers a rare combination of profitability and value in a sector where premium multiples remain the norm. Whether the market recognises that depends on what management says on Wednesday.
